books.name: Sahih al-Bukhari
books.note: The most rigorously selected of the collections, arranged by subject rather than by narrator.

books.name: Sahih Muslim
books.note: Noted for gathering the routes of each report together, so a matn can be read across its chains.

books.name: Sunan Abi Dawud
books.note: A collection of reports bearing on legal practice, with the compiler's own notes on their standing.

books.name: Jami' al-Tirmidhi
books.note: Marks the grade and the legal use of many of its reports, and names the authorities for its judgements.

books.name: Sunan an-Nasa'i
books.note: Tight in its conditions on narrators, and often fuller in chains than its counterparts.

books.name: Sunan Ibn Majah
books.note: The last of the six to be widely agreed on as a Sunan, and varied in grade across its chapters.

books.name: Musnad Ahmad
books.note: Arranged by the Companion who narrated, rather than by subject.

books.name: Sunan al-Darimi
authors: Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi
books.note: Counted with the six as one of the nine books; its compiler is not yet in this archive.

books.name: al-Muwatta'
books.note: The earliest surviving work to set hadith beside Madinan practice; filed here as a fiqh work, and counted among the nine books.

books.name: al-Risala
books.note: The early systematic statement of how the sources of law relate to one another, and of what makes a report acceptable.

books.name: al-Adab al-Mufrad
books.note: A collection on manners and conduct, gathered by the compiler of the Sahih.

books.name: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din
books.note: A work of religious practice and ethics that draws on hadith throughout; read alongside the collections rather than as one of them.

books.name: al-Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah
books.note: A short statement of creed that later commentaries took as a baseline.

books.name: al-Kitab
books.note: The founding description of Arabic grammar, and the work later grammars are written against.

books.name: Lisan al-Arab
books.note: A large dictionary of the Arabic tongue, still used to settle the sense of a word in a matn.

books.name: al-Fihrist
books.note: A catalogue of the books of the tenth-century Islamic world, and the reason many lost works are still known by name.

books.name: Jami' al-Bayan (Tafsir al-Tabari)
books.note: A tafsir built on the reports received for each verse, with the chains given and weighed.

books.name: Tafsir Ibn Kathir
books.note: A tafsir that reads each verse through the reports and the practice of the first generations.

books.name: The Qur'an
books.note: The primary text. Every citation in the archive is given by surah and verse, and no hadith is used to establish its text.

books.name: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah
books.note: The recension of Ibn Ishaq's biography that survives, and the backbone of the seerah in this archive.

books.name: Tarikh al-Rusul wa al-Muluk
books.note: An annalistic history from the beginning of time to 915 CE, quoting its reports with their chains.

books.name: Futuh al-Buldan
books.note: The conquests arranged region by region, with the terms on which each place came in.

books.name: al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya
books.note: A history from creation to the author's own day, strong on the reports and their criticism.

books.name: al-Kamil fi al-Tarikh
books.note: A general history valued for its account of the Crusades and of the Seljuk and Zangid states.

books.name: Kitab al-Ibar
books.note: A universal history whose introduction, the Muqaddimah, sets out how history should be written and checked.

books.name: al-Khitat (al-Mawa'iz wa al-I'tibar)
books.note: A topography of Egypt and Cairo: its mosques, madrasas, quarters and endowments.

books.name: Bada'i al-Zuhur
books.note: An eye-witness chronicle of Egypt to the Ottoman conquest of 1517.

books.name: al-Mukhtasar fi Akhbar al-Bashar
books.note: A summary history written by a prince of Hama who governed and fought in the period he describes.
sources: Abu al-Fida, al-Mukhtasar fi Akhbar al-Bashar

books.name: Akhbar Misr
books.note: An Egyptian chronicle, and one of the sources for the Fatimid period in Cairo.

books.name: Ahsan al-Taqasim fi Ma'rifat al-Aqalim
books.note: A geographer's survey of the Islamic lands, region by region, written from travel rather than from earlier books.

books.name: Siyar A'lam al-Nubala
books.note: A biographical dictionary of the notable figures of the tradition, with the author's own verdict on each.

books.name: al-Nawadir al-Sultaniyya
books.note: A life of Salah al-Din by a secretary and judge who served him and was present at his campaigns.

books.name: Nafh al-Tib
books.note: A history and anthology of al-Andalus, and the source through which much of its scholarship is known.

books.name: Baburnama
books.note: The founder of the Mughal empire's own memoir, from his Central Asian campaigns to his conquest of Delhi.

books.name: Tuzuk-i Jahangiri
books.note: The Mughal emperor Jahangir's own record of his reign.

books.name: Tevarih-i Al-i Osman
books.note: The earliest Ottoman chronicle of the house of Osman, beginning with the foundation of the beylik.

books.name: Kitab-i Cihan-numa
books.note: An Ottoman universal history; its account of the early sultans is the one later chronicles follow.

books.name: Tarikh-i Abu al-Fath
books.note: A life of Mehmed II by a secretary in his chancery, and the source for the 1453 campaign's own account.

books.name: History of Mehmed the Conqueror
books.note: A Greek account of the fall of Constantinople by a contemporary official who served the sultan afterwards.
sources: Kritovoulos, History of Mehmed the Conqueror

books.name: Tarikh-i Alam-ara-yi Abbasi
books.note: The court history of the Safavid shahs to the reign of Abbas I.
sources: Iskandar Beg Munshi, Tarikh-i Alam-ara-yi Abbasi

books.name: Akbarnama
books.note: The official history of Akbar's reign, written by his own secretary of state.

books.name: Muntakhab al-Lubab
books.note: A history of the Mughal empire through the reign of Aurangzeb and after.

books.name: Tarikh-i Mubarakshahi
books.note: A history of the Delhi sultanates, and a source for the end of the Sayyid and Lodi lines.

books.name: Nusretname
books.note: A court history of the later seventeenth century, covering the Ottoman campaigns in Europe.

books.name: Shah Jahan Nama
books.note: A court account of the reign of Shah Jahan, the emperor who built the Taj Mahal and Shahjahanabad.

books.name: Rawdat al-Safaviyya
books.note: An early Safavid chronicle of the dynasty's rise, written close to the events it records.

books.name: Aja'ib al-Athar fi al-Tarajim wa al-Akhbar
books.note: An Egyptian chronicle whose treatment of the French occupation is the fullest contemporary account in Arabic.

books.name: al-Musannaf
books.note: A large Yemeni collection arranged by subject, drawn on for the routes of the reports it gathers.

books.name: Musnad Abi Dawud al-Tayalisi
books.note: An early musnad arranged by the Companion who narrated it; its compiler is one of the archive's own transmitters.

books.name: Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah
books.note: A collection of reports the compiler judged sound, with his own reasoning set out for each.

books.name: al-Sunan al-Kubra
books.note: A vast collection organised around legal chapters, with the routes of each report given in full.

books.name: Muwatta' Muhammad al-Shaybani
books.note: The Hanafi recension of Malik's Muwatta', with the compiler's own additions on the same method.

books.name: Kitab al-Umm
books.note: Al-Shafi'i's teaching on law as his students recorded it, and the corpus in which his method is worked out.

books.name: al-Futuhat al-Makkiyya
books.note: A work of Sufi teaching that quotes hadith throughout; read with the collections rather than as one of them.

books.name: al-Risala al-Qushayriyya
books.note: A manual of Sufi practice and biography that grounds its teaching in the Qur'an and the reports.

books.name: Tarikh al-Ya'qubi
books.note: A history valued for its attention to the provinces, to geography and to dynastic administration.

books.name: Muruj al-Dhahab
books.note: A history of the Muslim world and its neighbours, written by a man who travelled in much of it.

books.name: al-Muqaddimah
books.note: The introduction to Ibn Khaldun's history, on how reports, dynasties and cities are formed and how they should be checked.

books.name: Mu'jam al-Buldan
books.note: A geographical dictionary of places, with the reports and poetry each one is known by.

books.name: Tuhfat al-Nuzzar (Ibn Battuta's Travels)
books.note: An account of thirty years of travel across Africa, Asia and the Indian Ocean, with the cities and shrines along the way.

books.name: al-Tabaqat al-Kubra
books.note: Biographical layers of the Companions and those who followed them; the earliest surviving work of its kind.

books.name: Tarikh Baghdad
books.note: A biographical dictionary of the scholars of Baghdad, and a monument of the discipline of transmitter criticism.

books.name: Tahdhib al-Kamal
books.note: The reference work on the narrators of the six collections: who they are, when they lived and who they heard from.

books.name: al-Muntaqa min Minhaj al-I'tidal
books.note: A summary of Ibn Taymiyya's critique of a polemical work, and a specimen of the archive's biographical method.
